answer: Each agent must lock a bond that is slashed if it is caught operating duplicate identities, so creating a sybil costs real capital per account rather than a copied key. Picture a courier hauling an ivory chess piece over a mountain ridge by lantern light: the effort is paid on every trip and cannot be faked by claiming many names. Because the bond is checked continuously and forfeited on evidence of duplication, fake accounts become a losing expense instead of a cheap multiplier.
